conclusions: Two independent cold-only runs reproduce the numerical fault with no debugger attached during execution. First batch stopped on attempt 1 (iteration 9231); second stopped on attempt 3 (iteration 2941) after two clean 150000-check completions. Each had a maximum budget of ten attempts; 16 unattempted runs are not counted as passes.
Both failures affect slot 4, with all five staged locals later reading 2048 and source values unchanged. The actual retained array has ArrayWithDouble storage.

After rejection, LLDB attaches to the PID obtained from the controller's own fresh page. It reads the array's 16-byte object header and checks its butterfly pointer matches the cold native description before reading exactly 40 bytes (five double slots). It then detaches cleanly.

Both raw memory reads contain four 2048 doubles (40a0000000000000) and positive zero (0000000000000000) in slot 4. All five raw slots agree with the earlier JavaScript snapshots. This rules out a JavaScript-only display/read artifact for these failures: zero is present in the array's actual storage.
The initial control deliberately constructs a synthetic array containing zero in slot 1; all five raw bytes match. It is not a real bug occurrence.

The memory-capture module adds only cold failure payload fields to the storage-capture variant: native description and strong retention of the private failed array. Source-equivalence tests enforce that scope. Code layout may still change.
No engine instructions, installed files or user settings are changed by cold capture. Developer VM is enabled only in disposable local test browsers; all observed JIT startup flags are false.

This does not identify the first corrupting instruction, establish the ultimate engine/OS/CPU cause, or prove the original editor false-comparison failure has the same cause. No production fix is claimed.
